explanation: As the lesson 'Single-Area OSPF Configuration and DR/BDR Elections' explains (chapter 'Wildcard Mask Usage in OSPF and ACLs', 18:22), 0 bits in the wildcard must match, so 0.0.255.255 requires the first two octets to be 10.1. Only 10.1.1.1 and 10.1.200.1 match; 10.2.x and 10.0.x fail the second octet.

stem: Four OSPF routers share one Ethernet segment. On R3, show ip ospf neighbor lists R1 as FULL/DR, R2 as FULL/BDR and R4 as 2WAY/DROTHER. What does the R4 entry indicate?
options: The hello timers on R3 and R4 do not match
Normal operation: DROTHER routers stay in 2-Way with each other and reach Full only with the DR and BDR
R4 has priority 0 and therefore cannot form an adjacency with any router
R3 and R4 are configured in different OSPF areas
explanation: As the lesson 'Single-Area OSPF Configuration and DR/BDR Elections' explains (chapter 'Verifying OSPF Routes and Neighbor Status', 38:32), Two-Way means basic communication without full adjacency, which is expected between two DROTHERs on a broadcast segment. Mismatched hello timers or areas would stop the routers from reaching 2-Way at all, and priority 0 still allows Full adjacencies with the DR and BDR.

stem: On a broadcast segment, R1 is DR, R2 is BDR and R3 is DROTHER. An engineer sets ip ospf priority 200 on R3's interface, but show ip ospf neighbor still shows R1 as DR. What explains this?
options: The DR election is non-preemptive, so R3 becomes DR only after the current DR and BDR are lost or the OSPF processes on the segment's routers are reset, for example with clear ip ospf process
Priority 200 is outside the valid range, so IOS rejected the command
The priority must be configured under router ospf, not on the interface
Running clear ip ospf process on R3 alone will immediately make R3 the DR
explanation: As the lesson 'Single-Area OSPF Configuration and DR/BDR Elections' explains (chapter 'Modifying DR/BDR Election with Priority Numbers', 63:32), the priority range is 0-255 and is set per interface, but a new priority does not displace an existing DR; clear ip ospf process forces a re-election. Resetting only R3 just brings it back as DROTHER, because R1 and R2 keep their roles.

stem: Two OSPF routers on the same link fail to become neighbors, and the engineer reviews how their router IDs were chosen. Which two statements about the OSPF router ID on Cisco IOS are correct? (Choose two)
options: Two neighbors with the same router ID still form a Full adjacency
Without a router-id command, the lowest IP address on an active physical interface is chosen
A router-id configured under the OSPF process takes precedence over any interface address
The router ID must be an address that is advertised and reachable in OSPF
Without a router-id command, the highest IP address on an up loopback interface is preferred over physical interface addresses
explanation: As the lesson 'Single-Area OSPF Configuration and DR/BDR Elections' explains (chapter 'OSPF Process ID and Router ID Uniqueness', 68:37), neighboring OSPF routers must have unique router IDs, and the ID is assigned automatically from IP addresses only if none is configured. IOS prefers a manual router-id, then the highest up loopback address, then the highest active physical address; the ID is only an identifier and need not be reachable.
